minutes.headline: Space-needs survey shows town departments need far less room than the committee's earlier 14,000-sq-ft plan
minutes.summary: The Building Design Committee spent the meeting reviewing department-by-department responses to its staff space-needs survey (town clerk, treasurer, HR, town manager, conservation, planning, facilities, building department, board of health, recreation), flagging where storage and interaction questions needed to be re-asked in clearer terms (e.g., "file cabinets" instead of square footage). No formal building or budget decision was made; the committee agreed to keep assessing needs independent of current buildings, standardize how storage is measured, and reconvene June 29th, while several members stressed the town currently has little appetite or capital funding for new construction.

budget_items.topic: Cost of new building storage space
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair noted that 500 square feet of storage in a new building translates into a large dollar figure, cautioning the committee that small square-footage numbers become much bigger costs when discussing new construction.

budget_items.topic: Prior building proposal vs. current survey estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted the space needs identified in the new staff survey come in well below his earlier per-person calculation, and well below the committee's previous proposal that was rejected by the town.
The town clerk's office was estimated at roughly 600 square feet for three staff, with the main gaps being vault space, counter space, and a private area for voting-related business.

The treasurer's office was reported at about 128 square feet for three employees, described as tight, with a need for more storage, a secure area for cash handling, and vault space; a member asked for actual square-footage or filing-cabinet estimates rather than vague terms.
HR's current space was reported at about 129 square feet for one employee, which the committee felt was adequate; a small amount of additional storage was requested.

The town manager's office and storage were estimated at roughly 450 square feet of office plus 120 square feet of storage, described as close to adequate, with a request for a private meeting room for up to six people.
Conservation's office and storage were estimated at about 187 square feet for one employee, with a request for a service counter and space to spread out plans with visitors.

The planning department reported about 750 square feet including a conference room, described as an inefficient layout; digitization was said to be reducing storage needs significantly and older records could move offsite.
Facilities reported about 160 square feet of office space at the Ritter building, with the main unmet need being dedicated shop/storage space, currently borrowed from DPW.

The building department reported about 350 square feet of office and counter space, with storage described in cubic feet rather than square feet, which the committee found hard to compare across departments.

budget_items.topic: Board of Health office and storage
budget_items.what_was_said: The Board of Health and a shared part-time staffer occupy about 179 square feet including fourteen filing cabinets, with digitization identified as a way to reduce future storage needs.

decisions.decision: Laura agreed to draft additional survey questions about how often staff interact with other departments/offices, to be sent through the town manager.

Committee agreed (per Chris's suggestion) to assess each department's space needs independent of whether Town Hall or the Ritter building currently houses them, rather than designing around existing buildings first.
Committee agreed to standardize future storage questions around number of filing cabinets (or filing method) and frequency of access, rather than square footage alone.
Next committee meeting set for June 29th.

what_happened.line: Staff space-needs survey estimates come in well below the committee's earlier, town-rejected 14,000-square-foot building proposal.
Committee agreed to size any future building around actual department needs rather than around Town Hall or the Ritter building's current layout.
Committee agreed to standardize how departments report storage, using filing-cabinet counts instead of vague square-footage estimates.
Members flagged that even small storage footage translates into large construction costs, and noted the town currently has little appetite or capital funding for new building.
No vote on a building plan or budget was taken; the committee set its next meeting for June 29th to continue the department-by-department review.

why_it_matters: Any future town building project and its price tag would ultimately need voter approval at town meeting, and this survey is shaping what that project would ask for.
A smaller space estimate than the rejected 14,000-square-foot plan could mean a cheaper future proposal, but no design or cost has been decided.

Departments named here -- town clerk, treasurer, HR, town manager, conservation, planning, facilities, building, board of health, recreation -- are the ones whose current offices and storage are under review.
